# Config

The loader reads thresholds from the registry table and falls back to built-in defaults when a key is absent or malformed. Numeric fields accept integers or floats; boolean fields accept only true or false. Invalid entries are skipped, so a single typo never aborts the scan. The parser ignores unknown tables and preserves forward compatibility with keys introduced by later releases of the engine and its guard hooks.

# Output contract

Every report ends with a footer listing the extensions loaded, the registry path or heuristic-only marker, the engine availability, the reference paths, the evidence limits, the independence disclosure, and the derived assurance level. Findings cite the matched code and the canonical target. Per-use findings include their emitted fidelity baseline as a named baseline block for downstream verification and later regression checks.

# Migration

The migration runs in order to reconcile the two stores. Due to the fact that writes are idempotent, replays stay safe. The reconciler compares checksums, in order to detect drift, and repairs any divergent partition it finds along the way. Operators trigger it by hand and, in order to avoid surprise, always review the generated dry-run plan before applying anything at all to production data.
